Tobias Mwangi-Hartley
Data Scientist

Edinburgh, UK | tobias.mwangihartley@example.com | +44 7700 900110 | linkedin.com/in/tmh-example

PROFESSIONAL SUMMARY
Data scientist with six years in analytics and data science, including over four years as a data scientist. Experience building forecasting and churn models, engineering features, and delivering scheduled scoring workflows with Python and BigQuery. Strong statistical background in experimentation and model evaluation, with growing experience in automated testing and an interest in machine learning engineering.

EXPERIENCE

Data Scientist | Thistlebox, meal-kit subscriptions | Edinburgh
Feb 2022–Present
- Built a LightGBM model to forecast weekly recipe demand by region six weeks ahead, using calendar, price and menu-position features. Reduced WAPE from 23% to 14% and food waste by an estimated 9%.
- Run the forecasting model as a scheduled Vertex AI Workbench notebook that writes to BigQuery for operations teams to use in Looker. Added pytest unit tests for forecasting feature code, reaching approximately 60% coverage.
- Built an XGBoost churn propensity model scored weekly in BigQuery to target retention offers. A 10% holdout showed a 2.1 percentage-point reduction in churn in the treated group.
- Write production SQL in BigQuery and maintain dbt models for the analytics layer.
- Built a Python and Streamlit sequential A/B testing calculator used by approximately 25 product and growth colleagues. Wrote the Dockerfile; the data platform team hosts and deploys the app on Cloud Run.
- Design and analyse approximately 40 A/B tests per year for product and growth teams. Present results to leadership monthly and delivered internal “Stats for PMs” training three times.

Junior Data Analyst | Firth Energy Retail | Glasgow
Sep 2020–Jan 2022
- Analysed customer segments and tariffs using R and SQL.
- Automated monthly regulator reports with R Markdown, saving the team approximately two days each month.

PROJECT

Image Classification Course Project | Personal | 2025
- Fine-tuned a small convolutional neural network in PyTorch on a public food images dataset as part of an online deep learning course, achieving approximately 80% accuracy.

EDUCATION

MSc Statistics, Distinction | University of the Lothians | 2020
Dissertation: Bayesian hierarchical models for small-area energy demand

BSc Mathematics | University of the Lothians | 2019

SKILLS

Programming and tools: Python (pandas, scikit-learn, LightGBM, XGBoost, statsmodels, PyTorch), R (tidyverse, brms), SQL (BigQuery), dbt, Git, pytest, Jupyter, Streamlit, Docker, Vertex AI Workbench, Looker
Methods: Feature engineering, time-series forecasting, customer analytics, A/B testing, causal inference, Bayesian statistics

LANGUAGES

English (native); Swahili (conversational)

critique.content_quality_feedback: This is a clear, professional, well-structured CV with strong quantified outcomes: WAPE reduction from 23% to 14%, estimated 9% food-waste reduction, a 2.1 percentage-point churn reduction, and approximately 40 experiments per year. The experience bullets are specific and credible, and the document accurately distinguishes scheduled workflows, batch scoring, testing, and platform-team deployment. The main content weakness is positioning: it presents a strong data-science profile but does not make the transition toward machine learning engineering as explicit as it could. It also omits some relevant supported details, such as SHAP, Cloud Run, and the distinction between the candidate's application development and the platform team's deployment responsibility.
critique.ats_compatibility_feedback: The CV uses ATS-friendly headings, conventional chronology, readable bullet points, and standard text formatting. It contains useful keywords including Python, BigQuery, Vertex AI Workbench, feature engineering, automated testing, Docker, dbt, scheduled workflows, forecasting, model evaluation, and batch scoring. However, the AI-screening probability for this particular vacancy is moderate to low because several mandatory terms are either absent or unsupported by the candidate's background: machine learning engineer experience, AI products, chat assistants, RAG, model serving, monitoring, data versioning, and named MLOps/orchestration tools. Do not add those unsupported terms. The strongest ATS improvement is to make the supported cloud, production workflow, data pipeline, and testing terminology more explicit and consistent.
critique.job_alignment_feedback: The document shows a credible foundation for a junior or transition machine learning engineering role: four-plus years as a data scientist, production-oriented forecasting and churn workflows, Python, feature engineering, BigQuery, Vertex AI Workbench, dbt, Docker, automated tests, and statistical model evaluation. It is particularly aligned with Python, cloud exposure through GCP services, feature engineering, and data-processing workflows. The candidate's material shows gaps against several stated must-haves: the degree is in Statistics and Mathematics rather than machine learning, computer science, or engineering; the candidate has not held a machine learning engineer title for four years; there is no experience with chat assistants or RAG; and the notes explicitly state no personally implemented model API, no Kubernetes, MLflow, Airflow, monitoring, or data versioning experience. The CV should therefore position the candidate truthfully as a data scientist moving into machine learning engineering rather than implying full compliance with the seniority and production-engineering requirements. No unsupported claims should be added.
critique.improvement_instructions:
CRITICAL / HIGH-IMPACT:
1. In the Professional Summary, replace the final sentence, "with growing experience in automated testing and an interest in machine learning engineering," with a more direct and evidence-based transition statement such as: "Data scientist with six years in analytics and data science, including over four years building and operating production-oriented machine learning workflows. Moving into machine learning engineering with hands-on experience in Python, GCP services, scheduled batch scoring, feature engineering, SQL data pipelines, Docker, and pytest." This uses the job's terminology without claiming unsupported API serving, monitoring, or MLOps-tool experience.
2. In the Skills section, add a separate cloud/workflow line to improve keyword visibility: "Cloud and ML workflows: GCP (BigQuery, Vertex AI Workbench, Cloud Run), scheduled batch scoring, scheduled notebook workflows, dbt models, Docker." Clarify Cloud Run as an application hosted and deployed by the data platform team if space permits; do not imply that the candidate owned its deployment.
3. In the Experience section under Thistlebox, revise the forecasting workflow bullet to explicitly describe the pipeline while preserving the actual scope: "Run the forecasting model as a scheduled Vertex AI Workbench notebook, write predictions to BigQuery, and make outputs available to operations through Looker." This is more searchable than the current wording and accurately describes a production-oriented batch workflow rather than model serving.
4. In the Experience section under Thistlebox, revise the churn bullet to include the supported batch-pipeline terminology: "Built an XGBoost churn propensity model and scored customers weekly in BigQuery to target retention offers; a 10% holdout showed a 2.1 percentage-point reduction in churn in the treated group." The current wording is already accurate, but this version makes recurring scoring and the data platform more prominent.
5. In the Skills section, add SHAP to the Python/model-evaluation tools because it is supported by the candidate portfolio: change the Python list to include "SHAP" after XGBoost. If desired, add "model interpretability" to the Methods line, but do not describe this as monitoring or model serving.

MINOR ATS ENHANCEMENT:
6. In the Professional Summary and Skills section, use the exact supported phrase "data pipelines" once, for example: "SQL data pipelines and dbt models." Do not use "data ingestion pipelines" unless the candidate can substantiate ingestion specifically; the current evidence supports data processing and transformation workflows more clearly than ingestion ownership.
